title: test-0002-GEN-GLOBAL
passage: Many people think the United Nations (UN) is a world government that makes laws every country must obey. However, the UN is actually an international organization where sovereign nations cooperate to maintain peace. It was not formed to fight wars, but to prevent them through diplomacy. Within the UN, the Security Council handles global security. For a resolution to pass here, all five permanent members must agree; if even one says "no," the resolution fails regardless of other votes. Specialized agencies like UNESCO and UNICEF are part of the UN system, not independent bodies. Similarly, the G20 is often misunderstood. It is not a part of the UN, nor does it include every country. The G20 consists of 19 countries and the European Union, making it a group of 20 members, not just 20 individual nations. During India’s 2023 presidency, the theme "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" showed that the G20 focuses on global well-being, not just trade and money. India used this platform to represent the Global South, proving that international bodies are about cooperation rather than forcing countries to follow orders.
summary: Many people think the UN is a world government that makes laws for everyone. India used this platform to represent the Global South, showing that international bodies help countries work together rather than just forcing them to follow orders.
